articles.title: The pest I’ll never forget: I awoke to the sound of my bedroom bin rustling
articles.summary: At first the mice were just a distant pitter-patter. But soon they had an unblinking confidence that they owned the entire house and all the food in it. Living in a nine-person house in Vancouver, Canada, far from my UK home, came with plenty of benefits. Cleanliness was not one of them.
body: In the winter of 2023, one of my housemates began to hear the sound of creatures rattling around in the ceiling of her basement room. The pitter-patters grew louder and louder; others began to report sightings from across the house. It wasn’t long before I was waking to the sound of my bedroom bin rustling. I had to accept it: we had mice.

When I saw my first mouse scuttling across the kitchen floor, my body filled with dread at the battle I knew we had ahead. Sleep quickly became a luxury. My housemate claimed she could hear hundreds of mice partying above her head. Frustrated with her inability to sleep, she would regularly hit her ceiling panels and be rewarded by a mouse falling on her face in return.

There was rarely a day when any food left in the cupboard hadn’t been gnawed through. I spent many mornings staring at my sourdough bread and questioning whether the large holes in it were from natural causes or mouse-made. I even began to believe I could recognise the taste of food that had also been sampled by our tiny friends. It all sounds mad, but it became hard to work out what was real or not when every time you walked into a room you were greeted by a squeal.
points: At first the mice were just a distant pitter-patter.
But soon they had an unblinking confidence that they owned the entire house and all the food in it.

articles.title: ‘To sleep in a sculpture is a wonderful idea’: a hike along Andy Goldsworthy’s epic art trail in Haute-Provence
articles.summary: A long-distance walking route in the south of France devised by the celebrated land artist offers intrepid hikers an opportunity to immerse themselves in nature and art. At 69, I had never hiked with a backpack and I had no idea what land art was.
body: First, I watch Rivers and Tides, a documentary on Goldsworthy’s work, and discover he has built exquisite ice sculptures and stone cairns in my own country, Canada. His work seems to speak to an older part of the soul. Then, I start walking up hills, gradually adding weights to my backpack until I can comfortably carry 9kg (20lb).

We meet in Digne-les-Bains, a bustling mountain town in the centre of the Unesco geopark of Haute-Provence, and the starting point for a 10-day, 150km (93-mile) hiking route that includes the possibility of staying overnight at seven reservable but free off-grid sleeping cabins. Goldsworthy worked alongside local teams to restore the abandoned shepherd huts, farmhouses, chapel and stone shelters, and created a site-specific artwork for each one. Over four days, we will visit three of these refuges and hike about 45km (28 miles).

articles.title: London Is So Back: Key Takeaways From Spring/Summer 2027
articles.summary: With renewed momentum on the ground and a more pragmatic approach to business, London Fashion Week saw a resurgence for SS27. These were the shifts industry professionals should note.
body: Burberry bookended the week with a show that was both parts kooky — featuring offbeat prints and badged designs — and commercially minded, primed with easygoing tailoring, track jackets, and hefty denim. A surprise cameo from rapper Central Cee gave the show a quintessentially British star factor, while the front row was curated to match this Made in Britain sensibility: Jason Statham, Stephen Graham, Kano, and Tems.

The BFC’s CEO, Laura Weir, also gave a notably upbeat speech, highlighting a shift in tactics she and her team have ushered in with the 2030 strategy, which focuses on clarifying the significance of British fashion on a global scale — giving the BFC and designer communities leverage with the UK government, partners, and international investment. The UK government’s Department for Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) has pledged £3 million for the next three rounds of NewGen — a support program for emerging design talent in London.

articles.title: My son has left home – and I feel full of complicated joy | Zoe Williams
articles.summary: I took him to university this weekend, and it reminded me of the exhilaration of suddenly having your own space, absolutely separate from your mother. When kids are small, and their expectations of an event diverge from yours in some important way, you feel terrible about it.
body: Then when they’re “adults”, your expectations diverge again. They thought you’d drop them at university and immediately leave, while you thought you’d unpack, and meet their flatmates, explore the city, and spin round a supermarket, then have a Nando’s, and maybe read a bedtime story, get chatting to the other parents and maybe all do karaoke? Well, then it’s time to manage your own disappointment, and the only thing to be said for that is that it’s way less bad than managing theirs.

When I went to university, my mum’s boyfriend drove me and there wasn’t room for her in the car, so it was a beautifully symmetrical event: I wanted him to leave and he wanted to leave. Then when she came to see me, I would count down the hours until she had to leave, and I used to love it when other people’s mums came to see them, because often they were nice, but, also, the schadenfreude was intense.

articles.title: The truth about Sean Combs: ‘No is not a stopping point for him’
articles.summary: Cheyenne Roundtree, an investigative reporter at Rolling Stone, was as shocked as anyone when allegations of rape and sexual abuse were made against the music mogul. Then she began digging into his past life.
body: For Cheyenne Roundtree, an investigative reporter at Rolling Stone, the civil lawsuit that dropped on Sean “Diddy” Combs in November 2023 seemed to come from nowhere. Filed by his ex-partner, the singer Cassie Ventura, it alleged that Combs had beaten and raped her, plied her with drugs and forced her into sexual encounters with male sex workers throughout their decade-long relationship.

Roundtree, along with much of the world’s media, was shocked. “I’d grown up in the era of Diddy and Cassie and viewed them as this power couple,” she says. “Her hit Me & U was my song. Diddy was this mogul – I knew him for the music – and she was this style inspiration, this beautiful, talented woman living an amazing life.”

“His attorneys took it head on,” says Roundtree. “They were saying: ‘We’re going to own the domestic violence, but that happened in the past – all that is locked in the 2010s and he has changed. He has become Love since then. [Combs had declared in November 2017 that he was renaming himself Love, or Brother Love.] He’s a new person, a father figure.’ But all these other lawsuits were telling a completely different story.”

articles.title: Inside the Dr. Martens Comeback
articles.summary: Following a recent decline, Dr. Martens has stabilized. In an exclusive interview, chief brand officer Carla Murphy unveils her action plan to reinvigorate the historic brand.
body: In two days, Dr. Martens will unveil the first major chapter in its ongoing face lift. Calling on a buzzy mix that spans It-girl Chloë Sevigny and comedian Naomi Watanabe through to musician Jordan Stephens, who will also be co-hosting a book club series, the brand will drop a cross-platform campaign rooted in one question: “What makes your sole bounce?”

The directive offers content creators, artists and muses a reason to pull apart their passions, forming snacky video formats, out-of-home advertising — coming to a sidewalk near you — and specialized activations. It also pays homage to the slogan — “With Bouncing Soles” — that appears on the heel tab of the brand’s signature boots.

articles.title: What Makes a Good Fashion Party?
articles.summary: As brands pour more money into fashion week events, the most successful nights are proving that curation and a reason to be there matter more than reach alone.
body: Fashion week without parties would be like a runway without clothes. The shows may be the official business of the week, but once the lights go down, the calendar fills up with store cocktails, intimate dinners, afterparties, brand activations and blockbuster raves — most of the time, all on the same night. In recent years, however, between the endless paid-for invites and choreographed step and repeats, going out can feel like clocking into another job.

From a brand’s perspective, Burkitt believes the party can offer something the runway cannot, which is perhaps why they’ve ballooned in popularity. “It takes a literal army of people to make these shows happen, and it’s over in 20 minutes. At least with a party, the DJ plays for about an hour minimum,” he says. “Having a place where you can get a thousand people through the door as opposed to just 200 at a fashion show, that exposes you to 10 times as many people posting about the brand, speaking about the brand with their mates at coffee the next morning, or being a part of it.”

articles.title: Can Photography Help Save the Earth’s Poles?
articles.summary: An industry-first partnership is tackling an age-old question in conservation, and a poignant one for the North and South Poles.
body: Ponant and Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI) were featured on Condé Nast Traveler' s Bright Ideas in Travel 2026. Read the full list of winners here.

Each time I’ve visited the Arctic or Antarctica on assignment—something I’ve had the privilege of doing twice this year alone—I’ve been humbled by the experience of attempting to accurately the document the sheer magnitude and fragility of the Earth’s polar regions. It’s one thing to photograph charismatic animals and marine megafauna, but with such wide, open landscapes you often need a human or animal subject to give the place scale. Most times, I’m left feeling like I only captured the tip of the iceberg, so to speak.

articles.title: Shanghai Fashion Week Unveils SS27 Schedule
articles.summary: Sportswear, showrooms, and supporting domestic talent are on the agenda for this Shanghai Fashion Week season.
body: Shanghai Fashion Week (SHFW) is betting on a more connected fashion ecosystem as it unveils its Spring/Summer 2027 schedule. The upcoming edition, running from October 8-16, will feature more than 80 runway shows and presentations across the city.

The designer schedule remains anchored by Shanghai’s independent fashion scene. Chinese designer brand Hemu will open the week on October 8, marking its 15th SHFW appearance. Established names including Xiaoli, Staffonly, Comme Moi, Shuting Qiu and Short Sentence will return, alongside a younger generation of independent labels.

The underlying message from organizers is straightforward: “local is international”. For this edition, that increasingly means combining Chinese creative talent and global fashion businesses in the same commercial ecosystem, rather than measuring success by the number of foreign names on the calendar.

articles.title: Here's What It's Like Shadowing a Blacksmith at Ashford Castle in Ireland—and How to Book the Experience Yourself
articles.summary: Writer Sarah Wood González visited the Guinness family’s former Irish estate—now one of Ireland's most iconic castle hotels—to try her hand at blacksmithing.
body: I can’t stop talking about blacksmithing. Any time I’ve run into someone in the last year, I’ve found some way to bring it up. Perhaps it’s a symptom of my obsession with the Middle Ages, or an effect of my brother being a welder, or maybe a function of my interest in age-old crafts as a way to counterbalance my anxiety about the unknown future.

That’s all to say, when I learned that Ashford Castle —the historic Guinness family estate turned iconic luxury hotel in County Mayo, Ireland —offers an experience where you can shadow a blacksmith for a day, I leapt at the opportunity. I booked the “Fire & Wood” itinerary within the hotel's Meet the Makers program, designed to help guests connect with authentic local crafts and culture, as part of an August stay with my mom. Next thing I knew, I was flying out to the Irish countryside.

articles.title: Savory Dutch Baby
articles.summary: Is there any time of day when a pancake isn’t welcome at the table? What about a Savory Dutch Baby that mixes up in seconds? Didn’t think so.
body: Essentially a giant popover, this savory Dutch baby emerges from the oven dramatically puffed, with crisp edges and a tender, eggy center. A blender makes quick work of the batter, while a little cornstarch helps create that contrast in textures. Don’t be alarmed when it begins to deflate after leaving the oven—that’s exactly what it’s supposed to do.
Top your Dutch baby with fried eggs, avocado, and shaved ham; smoked salmon, crème fraîche, and sliced scallions; or sautéed kale, crispy bacon, and aged cheddar.

A properly preheated skillet is key: This recipe heats the pan in a 450° oven for at least 25 minutes so the batter starts cooking as soon as it hits the surface. Room-temperature ingredients and whipping plenty of air into the eggs also encourage a good rise. And remember, your Dutch baby will naturally deflate after it comes out of the oven.

A blender quickly incorporates air into the eggs, helping the Dutch baby puff. No blender? Several Bon Appétit readers have successfully made this recipe using a whisk; beat the eggs vigorously until very frothy before adding the remaining ingredients.
